business_problem: Atlassian needed to upgrade its Rovo agent platform so it could handle enterprise-grade scale and quality, because lenient tool schemas in the legacy model were allowing subtle errors and limiting confidence in production rollouts.
solution_summary: Atlassian migrated its Rovo personal assistant and agent platform to Gemini 3 Flash to improve both agent reliability and production scale. During evaluation, the team discovered that Gemini 3 Flash enforced stricter tool-schema behavior than its prior model, which forced Atlassian to tighten tool definitions and eliminate silent failures that had previously slipped through. The company then rolled the model out in phases, using an opt-in toggle so customers could switch agents gradually while offline and online evaluation results were tracked closely. This combination of schema refinement, controlled migration, and Google Cloud's resilient infrastructure let Atlassian scale from a single invocation to more than 200,000 daily invocations in six weeks while preserving the responsiveness needed for simple requests and deeper multi-loop reasoning for complex enterprise tasks.

data_flow: User requests enter the Rovo agent platform, are handled by Gemini 3 Flash against stricter tool schemas, pass through evaluation gates during phased rollout, and then return either quick responses or deeper multi-loop reasoning results depending on task complexity.
business_outcome: Atlassian raised offline pass rates to 85%, boosted online agent success to 80%, moved nearly half of customers in two weeks, and scaled the platform to over 200,000 daily invocations in six weeks.
